title: Flag Well-Formed SKUs
description:
Every SKU must follow the format: **exactly two uppercase letters, a hyphen, then exactly four digits** — for example `AB-1234` or `XY-0099`.

Write a query that returns all products with columns `id`, `name`, and `is_valid`, where `is_valid` is `1` if the SKU matches the format and `0` otherwise.

Return the result in any order.
hint: Compute a boolean flag in the SELECT list with CASE WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(...) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END. `{2}` and `{4}` fix the exact lengths.
outputExplanation:
- `AB-1234` (Socks) — 2 uppercase letters, hyphen, 4 digits. `is_valid = 1`. ✓
- `XY-0000` (Hat) — leading zeros are still valid digits. `is_valid = 1`. ✓
- `ab-1234` (Shirt) — lowercase letters; the pattern requires uppercase only. `is_valid = 0`. ✗
- `AB-1` (Scarf) — only 1 digit after the hyphen; exactly 4 are required. `is_valid = 0`. ✗
- `AB12-345` (Glove) — digits before the hyphen break the two-letter prefix rule. `is_valid = 0`. ✗

All five rows are returned with their flag.
